question: The analysis of the data obtained from cases of Ebola virus disease in Guinea and Sierra Leone, allows us to affirm that:

options.opa: The mortality of the infection exceeds 85%.
options.opb: The treatment is based on support measures (hydroelectrolitic replenishment i.v. and antibiotics).
options.opc: More than half of the cases correspond to health personnel.
options.opd: Gastrointestinal hemorrhage is a common cause of mortality.

analysis: The analysis of Ebola virus disease cases in Guinea and Sierra Leone indicates that the mortality rate can exceed 70% but is not consistently above 85%. Treatment primarily involves supportive care rather than antibiotics, as antibiotics do not treat viral infections. A significant proportion of cases do involve health personnel due to their exposure in healthcare settings, but it is not more than half. Gastrointestinal hemorrhage is indeed a common symptom but not the primary cause of mortality. Mortality rates are generally higher in older adults rather than adolescents.
